approach.why: Two things set out to be done: close the held window's two oracle holes, and move the three Playwright lanes onto the testing-runtime standard. Both are done in a way that works. Oracles: parse_schema now returns a named-FK Schema (explicit CONSTRAINT or pg_default_name with NAMEDATALEN truncation) and models DROP/RENAME CONSTRAINT, DROP [COLUMN] and DROP TABLE, failing closed on an unresolvable name (oracle.py:509-535, 561-597, 722-738); host-tenant-binding Probe E scans every .nest/.nest_service, fails closed on a non-literal prefix and compares path params by position (oracle.py:643-706, 724-726). Verified here, not taken on trust: all three mutations.py runners exit 0 on this tree (erasure 10/10 red incl. G1/G2, host-binding 6/6 red incl. H5/H6, moderation 1/1 red; clean and restored copies exit 0), and both oracles exit 0 on the real tree. Playwright: the five _liveness files are byte-identical across admin-ui, marketing, widget and ~/.claude/templates/testing/playwright (md5 match), every spec in the three lanes imports test/expect from the fixture (grep: none left on @playwright/test for test), timeouts stay 0, and the test-liveness oracle passes on this tree. Test lens: each spec's change is the import line only; liveness.ts re-exports Playwright's expect unchanged (line 21) and test is base.extend (line 172), so no assertion, cell or comparison was loosened. The window's own composition is consistent: metadata.testServer commands match the package scripts (admin-ui dev=vite on 14204 strictPort; widget vite preview --outDir . on 14206; marketing preview on 14222 in package.json, astro.config.mjs and playwright.config.ts alike), and test_queue.py resolves .cmd on win32 via proc.resolve, so the old webServer .cmd workaround is not needed. ci-local.sh's .env read is guarded (only when DATABASE_URL is unset and .env exists; strips CR; CI unaffected). The concerns below are a stale instruction the window made wrong, a documented promise the standard does not keep off-ULDF, and a lane left unrun.
